title: Pride is humbled, and the humble heart is never disgraced
subtitle: Al-Muzill: why Allah humbles the arrogant, and why this name protects the believer
intro: Al-Muzill (المذل) means the Humbler: the One who removes false honour from those who choose arrogance, oppression and rebellion, always by His justice and wisdom. Said together with Al-Mu'izz, it means no tyrant keeps the last word, and no one can truly disgrace a heart that Allah has honoured.

root.sense: Dhull is lowness and yielding. A path worn smooth by many feet is called dhalul, tame and easy, and Allah made the earth dhalul for us to walk on (67:15). Idhlal is to bring someone low and break their stubbornness. The root holds both the broken pride of the arrogant and the gentle lowliness of a servant before his Lord.

row.title: Allah has disgraced me
sub: a loss, a failure, a shame

row.title: A trial is not a disgrace
sub: He humbles arrogance, not His servants

knowing: Al-Muzill is the One who humbles. The dua the Quran teaches says: You honour whom You will and You humble whom You will; in Your hand is all good (3:26). Notice how it ends: all good is in His hand, even in this. The name is in the well-known list in Jami' al-Tirmidhi, and scholars insist it should not be mentioned alone, only together with Al-Mu'izz, because together they describe full sovereignty over honour.

{idea}His humbling is justice, never cruelty.{/idea} He does not humble the poor, the sick or the weak for being weak. He humbles what rises up against Him: arrogance, oppression, mockery of the truth, the hand that crushes others. He strips away a borrowed honour to break a tyrant's pride, so that the world is not left to bullies.

Hardship is not humiliation. Prophets were mocked, exiled and wounded, and Allah never disgraced them; they were the most honoured of people. A believer can lose money, health or reputation and remain honoured in His sight. Even for someone who sinned, being humbled can be mercy: a fall that breaks pride and sends them back to Him in repentance is far better than a worldly honour that leads to ruin.
seeing: History is full of people who thought their power was permanent: Pharaoh, who claimed lordship; Qarun, who said his wealth came from his own knowledge. Both were brought low in a single moment. And there were those who stood over the bodies of believers, certain they had won. On the Day of Resurrection there will be no armies and no titles, only servants standing before their Lord.

The same pattern appears in small lives. A person who builds status by mocking others, by chasing fame at any cost, by trading faith for approval, often finds that the very thing they leaned on gives way. Seeking honour anywhere other than with Allah is the road to humiliation. Yet the believers have known periods of weakness in history too, and those were tests, not signs that Allah had disgraced them.
trusting: Fear of humiliation drives so much of what we do: hiding mistakes, pleasing people, staying silent when we should speak. If only Allah truly humbles, then people cannot disgrace you while you hold on to Him. {reward}You can stop living in terror of what others might say.{/reward}

If someone is oppressing you, this name tells you the matter is not unseen. Allah is not unaware of what the wrongdoers do; He only gives them time (14:42). And look inward too: {trap}arrogance is the door through which humiliation enters a life.{/trap} The one who willingly lowers himself before Allah in prostration is the one He raises.
loving: Because He humbles the proud, the weak are never left without a defender, and the playing field is level in the end. And because He gives honour to whoever humbles himself before Him, the door is open to every person, whatever their past. {idea}You love Him for being the One who will not let cruelty win and who never shames a servant who comes back to Him.{/idea}
now: A clip of a mistake you made at work is going round the group chat, and every notification makes your stomach drop. You feel exposed and small. Al-Muzill humbles arrogance, not honest people who stumble, and your standing with Him has not moved. Own the mistake simply, fix what you can, and stop refreshing the chat.
old: Being embarrassed or looked down on feels like proof that I have lost my worth.
new: Only Allah humbles, and He humbles pride and injustice; a sincere servant who falls is not disgraced in His sight.
try: When someone belittles you today, pause before answering, say nothing harsh, and remind yourself who alone gives and removes honour.

dua.text: O Allah, You are Al-Mu'izz and Al-Muzill. Honour me through obedience and never humble me through my sins. Keep arrogance far from my heart, and do not disgrace me in this life or on the Day of Resurrection.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name only together with Al-Mu'izz, as the Quranic dua in 3:26 does, asking for protection from the disgrace that comes through pride and sin.

pairs.why: He honours and He humbles: the two names are said together and describe His full control over honour.
Greatness belongs to Him alone, so He humbles any creature that claims it for itself.
His humbling is never arbitrary; Al-Adl means it falls only where it is deserved.

faq.a: Al-Muzill means the Humbler or the One who abases. Allah removes false honour from those who are arrogant, oppressive and rebellious, by His justice and wisdom. The name is in the well-known list in Jami' al-Tirmidhi and is always mentioned together with Al-Mu'izz, the Bestower of Honour.

Allah does not humble anyone unjustly or for being weak. He humbles arrogance, oppression and rebellion against Him, which protects the oppressed and keeps tyrants from having the last word. Sometimes being humbled is also a mercy that breaks a person's pride and brings them back to Him in repentance.

faq.q: Can Al-Muzill be said on its own?
faq.a: Scholars advise mentioning Al-Muzill together with Al-Mu'izz, never alone, as the Quran does in 3:26: You honour whom You will and You humble whom You will. Together the two names express perfect control and wisdom, while one alone could give an incomplete picture.
